sentences.text: This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 06.10.2018 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi, in MVC No.936 of 2017.
2. The claimant met with an accident on 17.02.2017 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the NEKRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-42/ F-796 and sustained grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.14,50,000/-.

3. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.7,31,800/-
with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation NC: 2025:KHC-K:6628 HC-KAR and directed the respondent-Corporation to deposit the same.

4. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal,
in which it is contended that, the doctor assessed the disability at 99% to the whole body, but the Tribunal has taken the disability at only 20%; the doctor estimated the cost for removal of implants as Rs.40,000/-, but the Tribunal has granted only Rs.25,000/-; the amount awarded under other heads is meagre; he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken his income only at Rs.6,500/- per month.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6.
Though the appellant stated that he was an agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, he has not produced any income proof.

Therefore, as the accident is of the year 2017, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka NC: 2025:KHC-K:6628 HC-KAR State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.10,250/- per month.

As he was aged 25 years, the multiplier was Laxman vs The Md Nekrtc on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163731453/
2 rightly taken as '18'.
The appellant has sustained fracture of right distal femur and fracture shaft of tibia right.

The X-rays show the old fracture of lower end shaft of right femur with internal fixation plate and screws seen in situ and old fracture of lower third shaft of right tibia and fibula with internal fixation rod and screws seen in situ.
The doctor has assessed the disability at 99%.
1/3rd of the same comes to 33%.
Hence, this Court finds it reasonable to taken the disability at 33% instead of 20% taken by the Tribunal.

Thus, the loss of future earnings is:
Rs.10,250 x 12 x 18 x 33% = 7,30,620/-.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.2,90,000/- towards medical expenses as per the relevant records and it needs no interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6628 HC-KAR 8.
The Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.35,000/- towards loss of amenities and the same needs no interference.
9. The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 76 days.

Considering the period of hospitalisation,
this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.40,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
10. Further, as per the evidence of PW.2-doctor, the appellant is entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- for removal of implants.
11. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of six months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.61,500/-
(Rs.10,250 x 6) for loss of income during laid up period.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6628 HC-KAR 12.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.75,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.2,90,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.7,30,620/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.61,500/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.40,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.35,000/-
Removal of implants Rs.40,000/-
Total Rs.12,72,120/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.7,31,800/-
Enhancement Rs.5,40,320/-
Laxman vs The Md Nekrtc on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163731453/
3
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,40,320/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

13. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.5,40,320/- with interest at NC: 2025:KHC-K:6628 HC-KAR 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iii) The respondent-Corporation is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
